# S3: Astro and a root index.html and .nojekyll

- Date: 2026-10-04
- Result: partial. The local half passes, with one dev-only quirk. The GitHub legacy half is pending the owner's approval of a throwaway repository.
- Decision: Keep the plan. The starter ships a root `index.html` ("Almost there") and an empty `.nojekyll`, and the theme needs no code for either. The theme never links to `/index.html`, because `url('/')` gives `/`. Revisit this decision once the GitHub half has run.

The spike was a throwaway project in `spikes/s3` (gitignored). It used Astro 7.3.5 (Vite 8.3.2), Node 22.22.3 and npm 10.9.8, with the settings `defineSiteConfig()` will use: `build.format: 'preserve'`, `trailingSlash: 'ignore'` and `devToolbar` off. It had four pages (`index`, `about`, `writing/index`, `404`) and `public/favicon.svg`. The root `index.html` was a realistic draft of the setup page: noindex, plain text, and an inline script that builds the Pages settings link from `location.hostname`. `run.mjs` builds and serves the project four times: at base `/` (a user site) and `/demo` (a project site), each with the two root files absent and then present. Each time it hashes every file in `dist/`, compares the build and dev logs, and requests 13 URLs twice. The first request uses `Accept: */*`, as a script would. The second sends a browser's `Accept: text/html…`, because Astro's dev route guard only acts on that header. Three smaller scripts covered what remained. `browser.mjs` drives the installed Google Chrome 154 through `playwright-core` 1.63.0. `hmr-timing.mjs` listens on the HMR socket while each file is edited. `control.mjs` checks an ordinary root file, `LICENSE`. One detail of the method matters. When Astro 7.3.5 detects a coding agent, it moves `astro dev` into the background with JSON logs. So every run used a minimal environment (`PATH`, `HOME`, `ASTRO_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1`) plus `--ignore-lock`, which behaves like a person's terminal.

**Build and preview.** At both bases, `dist/` is byte-identical with and without the files: same file list, same hashes, and `diff -r` prints nothing. The build logs are identical too. `dist/index.html` is the Astro home page, and `dist/.nojekyll` does not exist. `astro preview` serves `dist/`, so it is unaffected as well.

**Dev.** Every page URL gives the same status and the same body bytes either way, including `/`, `/about`, `/about.html`, `/writing/`, `/writing/index.html`, the 404 page, `/favicon.svg` and everything under `/demo/`. There are no new warnings, errors or restarts. Three things do differ, all in dev only:

1. **`/index.html` in a browser at base `/`.** A browser navigation shows Astro's built-in "404: Not found" page instead of the home page. The cause is Astro 7's dev route guard (`astro/dist/vite-plugin-astro-server/route-guard.js`). It answers 404 to any `text/html` request whose path is a file at the project root outside `src/` and `public/`, and `/index.html` now resolves to the root file. A `fetch` with `Accept: */*` still gets the home page. At base `/demo`, `/demo/index.html` still serves the home page, and `/index.html` was a 404 already, because it is outside the base.
2. **`/.nojekyll`.** Vite serves it as an empty JavaScript module (200, `text/javascript`) instead of letting Astro return the site's 404 page. A browser request at base `/` gets the route guard's 404 instead. This is generic Vite behaviour: a root `LICENSE` behaves exactly the same, and so do `/package.json` and `/astro.config.mjs`.
3. **Editing either file while dev is running.** Vite treats a changed root `.html` file as a full reload of every open page, because the client special-cases `/index.html`. A changed `.nojekyll` reloads the page zero to two times, depending on timing, just as `LICENSE` does. The content is unchanged either way, and nobody edits these files during normal work.

None of these changes `dist/` or any URL the theme generates.

The code behind difference 1, from Astro 7.3.5. The check below runs only for `text/html` requests without a query string:

```js
// astro/dist/vite-plugin-astro-server/route-guard.js (excerpt)
if (fsInfo.existsInPublic || fsInfo.existsInSrc) return { action: "next" };
if (fsInfo.existsAtRootAsFile) return { action: "block", pathname };   // -> notFoundTemplate, 404
```

And behind difference 3, from Vite 8.3.2's client:

```js
// vite/dist/client/client.mjs, case "full-reload"
if (pagePath === payloadPath || payload.path === "/index.html" || ...) pageReload();
```

## If the dev quirk ever matters

`fix.config.mjs` in the spike shows a dev-only fix that works. It is a Vite plugin (`apply: 'serve'`, `enforce: 'post'`) whose post `configureServer` hook unshifts a middleware that rewrites `/index.html` to `/`. That puts it in front of Astro's route guard. With it in place, a browser `GET /index.html` returns the home page, and `/`, `/about` and `/.nojekyll` are unchanged. It is not adopted, because nothing links to `/index.html` and the theme should not carry code for a URL nobody uses. Add it to the theme's integration only if a test or a user report needs it.

## Pending: the GitHub half

This half is not run yet. It needs the owner's approval to create a throwaway `<owner>.github.io` repository in the sandbox organization, so that GitHub auto-enables legacy branch mode. Then check two things: that the classic build is green with `.nojekyll` present, and that the site serves the "Almost there" page with its settings link. This is the same as M8 scenario (c). If it fails, the fallback from the plan applies: serve the page from `docs/` with legacy source `/docs`, or drop the safety net and rely on the README. Locally, a `docs/index.html` would behave the same way as the root file. `astro build` would ignore it, and only a browser request in dev for `/docs/index.html` would hit the route guard.

## GitHub half

- Date: 2026-10-04
- Result: not run yet. The template is prepared; generating the `<owner>.github.io` copy is blocked on the owner (same reason as S5's "Pending").
- Decision: unchanged. Revisit once `hangfolio/hangfolio.github.io` has been generated from the template.

**What was done.** `hangfolio/spike-template` gained the two root files on branch `s3-root-files` (commit `3c484d3`: the "Almost there" page from the local half, unchanged, and an empty `.nojekyll`), merged into `main` with a local `--no-ff` merge (`2b28091`) pushed over SSH. Its **Deploy site** runs went green on both the branch (https://github.com/hangfolio/spike-template/actions/runs/37223603361) and `main` (https://github.com/hangfolio/spike-template/actions/runs/37223604511). On the GitHub runner, as locally, Astro ignored both files: the build reported 2 pages and `dist/` held only the Astro output.

```
# build / build, run 37223604511 (template, Pages off)
2 page(s) built
$ find dist -type f | sort
dist/about.html
dist/index.html
dist/style.css
```

**Why the copy was not generated.** `hangfolio.github.io` is the only repository name that gets the org-site behaviour, and the repository cannot be deleted afterwards. A generated copy's "Initial commit" is authored with the generating account's web commit email, which is currently a personal address that must not appear in project repositories, so generating now would publish it permanently. A pushed copy (as in S4 to S6) would avoid the email but would use up the only org-site name without answering the actual question: whether GitHub auto-enables Pages for a repository *generated* from a template. So both were left alone.

**To finish.** After the owner turns on *Keep my email addresses private*: generate `hangfolio/hangfolio.github.io` from `hangfolio/spike-template` (public, default branch only); read `GET /repos/hangfolio/hangfolio.github.io/pages` for `build_type` and `source`; watch `pages/builds/latest` and request `https://hangfolio.github.io/` for "Almost there"; record what the **Deploy site** run does in that state; switch with `PUT .../pages -f build_type=workflow`, re-run, and confirm the Astro home page replaces the setup page; then unpublish Pages (`DELETE .../pages`) and archive the repository for later reuse as the demo site.

## Email reason cleared

- Date: 2026-10-04
- Result: not run yet (unchanged).
- Decision: unchanged.

The owner turned on *Keep my email addresses private*. A private test copy, `hangfolio/spike-email-check`, generated from `spike-template` showed that a generated "Initial commit" is now authored with the account's `users.noreply.github.com` address and carries no denylist term (details in S5, "Generated copy"). So the email reason in "Why the copy was not generated" no longer applies, and the steps in "To finish" can run. They were not run on this date.
